title: Compatible strict localizations of a regular morphism
statement:
Let $h:Y\to X$ be a regular morphism between Noetherian excellent schemes [def-exc-excellent-ring]: it is flat with fibres remaining regular after every finite extension of their residue fields [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. For a geometric point $\bar y$ over $\bar x$, with the specified map of geometric points over $h$, let $Y_{(\bar y)}$ and $X_{(\bar x)}$ be the strict localizations [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. The induced local morphism
$$h_{(\bar y,\bar x)}:Y_{(\bar y)}\longrightarrow X_{(\bar x)}$$
is regular and both schemes are Noetherian excellent. For any point $v$ of $Y_{(\bar y)}$ with image $u$ in $X_{(\bar x)}$ and images $y\in Y$, $x\in X$, the local fibre dimensions agree:
$$\dim\mathcal O_{(Y_{(\bar y)})_u,v}=\dim\mathcal O_{Y_x,y}.$$
Dimension means local-ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. The analogous assertions hold for ordinary localizations at compatible points. If $C\hookrightarrow X_{(\bar x)}$ is a closed subscheme, then $Y_{(\bar y)}\times_{X_{(\bar x)}}C\to C$ is regular and its source and target are Noetherian excellent.

source.place: Expose XVII, reductions at the start of Lemma 4.3.2.1 and Lemmas 4.3.2.3–4.3.2.4; algebraic local inputs: Stacks more-algebra.tex Tags 07C0 (lemma-regular-local), 07C1 (lemma-regular-base-change), 06LJ (lemma-henselization-noetherian), 06LN (lemma-henselization-regular). The compatible strict-local fibre-dimension assertion is the local-model formulation used in those reductions.

proof.text: Write $x_0,y_0$ for the images of the specified geometric points $\bar x,\bar y$ (distinct from the variable points $x,y$ in the conclusion); thus $h(y_0)=x_0$. Choose an affine open $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0\subset X$ containing $x_0$ and an affine open $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}S_0\subset h^{-1}(U_0)$ containing $y_0$, and let $\mathfrak p_0\subset A_0$, $\mathfrak q_0\subset S_0$ be the primes of $x_0,y_0$. Since the schemes are Noetherian excellent, $A_0$ and $S_0$ are Noetherian excellent rings. Put $R=(A_0)_{\mathfrak p_0}=\mathcal O_{X,x_0}$ and $S=(S_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}=\mathcal O_{Y,y_0}$; these are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] (the finite type $A_0$-algebra $A_0$ and the multiplicative subset $A_0\setminus\mathfrak p_0$; likewise for $S_0$), in particular Noetherian local rings. Let $A$ and $B$ be the coordinate rings of $X_{(\bar x)}$ and $Y_{(\bar y)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. In [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples], take the scheme $X$ and the chosen $U_0$. Its initiality and diagram equivalence, passed to the small representatives fixed in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], identify $A$, compatibly with the legs, with the vertex of a universal cocone of the etale residue triples of $(A_0,\mathfrak p_0,K)$, where $K$ is the separable closure of $\kappa(x_0)$ in the field of $\bar x$. The composites $A_0\to B'\to A$ along the legs are one map $b_X:A_0\to A$, and the structural morphism $j_X$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map] is $\operatorname{Spec}b_X$ followed by $U_0\subset X$. Apply [lem-sbc-etale-triples-localized-strict-henselization] to this cocone and $b_X$. It gives an $R$-algebra structure on $A$ with $A_0\to R\to A$ equal to $b_X$, and makes $A$ an algebraic strict henselization of $R$ relative to a separable closure $L$ of $R/\mathfrak m_R$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. The pair category of [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization] for $(R,L)$ is isomorphic, compatibly with the forgetful diagrams, to the triple category of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] for $(R,\mathfrak m_R,L)$. An $R$-algebra map $\chi:S'\to L$ has prime kernel $\mathfrak q'$, which lies over $\mathfrak m_R$ because $R\to L$ factors through $R/\mathfrak m_R$, and $\chi$ induces a $\kappa(\mathfrak m_R)$-algebra map $\phi:\kappa(\mathfrak q')\to L$. Conversely $(S',\mathfrak q',\phi)$ gives $\chi=S'\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')\xrightarrow{\phi}L$, and the two morphism conditions agree. Hence $A$ is $R$-isomorphic to the colimit $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ of that lemma: $A$ is a local ring, $R\to A$ is a filtered colimit of etale $R$-algebras, and $\mathfrak m_A\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$. The same argument for $Y$, $V_0$, $\bar y$ gives $b_Y:S_0\to B$, an $S$-algebra structure on $B$ with $S_0\to S\to B=b_Y$, and $B\cong S^{\mathrm{sh}}$ over $S$. Since $R$ and $S$ are Noetherian, [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] makes $A$ and $B$ Noetherian (transported along these isomorphisms). [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](3) gives the local map $A\to B$ with $j_X\circ\operatorname{Spec}(A\to B)=h\circ j_Y$. Both composites carry $\operatorname{Spec}B$ into the affine open $U_0$, because $j_Y$ factors through $V_0\subset h^{-1}(U_0)$. So on global sections over $U_0$ the ring maps $A_0\to A\to B$ and $A_0\to S_0\to S\to B$ coincide. Both $R\to A\to B$ and $R\to S\to B$ extend this common map along the localization $A_0\to R$, so they are equal. No finite-type assumption on $h$ has been introduced.

proof.text: Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples](1) express $R\to A$ and $S\to B$ as filtered colimits of etale $R$-, respectively $S$-algebras. They are ind-etale, hence weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. Apply [lem-exc-weakly-etale-excellent] separately to $R\to A$ and $S\to B$, with the Noetherian targets supplied by step 1: $A,B$ are excellent. Their spectra are Noetherian excellent schemes. In particular the multiplication $A\otimes_R A\to A$ is flat, as asserted by the definition of weak etaleness [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra].

source.place: Tags 04GP and 097N (ind-etale implies weakly etale); excellence supplied by Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Theorem 5.3(iv), through the cited existing DAG node

proof.text: Since $h$ is regular, its stalk map $R\to S$ is regular; on affine neighbourhoods this is [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal]. By Step 1, $B$ is the colimit of the etale $S$-algebras $S'$ of the triple diagram of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] for $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$. Replace that diagram by an equivalent small full subcategory of representatives: etale $S$-algebras are finitely presented, so they have a set of isomorphism classes, and each carries a set of triples. This subcategory is small, nonempty and filtered, and has the same colimit. Each $S\to S'$ has etale spectrum map, so it is an etale ring map in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine]: $S'$ is finitely presented, $H_1(L_{S'/S})=0$ and $\Omega_{S'/S}=0$. The zero module is finite projective, so $S\to S'$ is smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Each fibre ring of $S\to B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian], since $B$ is Noetherian. Therefore [lem-per-smooth-colimit-regular] gives regularity of $S\to B$. The composite $R\to B$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition]: its additional Noetherian-fibre hypothesis again follows from [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian].

source.place: Tags 07C0 (lemma-regular-local), 07EP (lemma-colimit-smooth-regular), 07QI (lemma-regular-composition); algebra.tex Definitions 00T2 and 00U1 (etale ring maps are smooth)

proof.text: The composite $R\to B$ is flat by step 3. Flat base change [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] gives a flat map $A\to A\otimes_R B$. Apply [lem-per-flat-tensor-scalar-comparison] with its $(R,S,T,U)=(R,A,A,B)$, using the flat multiplication from step 2: $A\otimes_R B\to A\otimes_A B\cong B$ is flat. The last isomorphism sends $a\otimes b$ to $ab$, with inverse $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. Its composite with $A\to A\otimes_R B$ is the specified map $A\to B$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp] makes that map flat.

source.place: Weak-etale flat-diagonal argument; Mathlib RingTheory/RingHom/Flat.lean:250–256; flat base change and composition (Stacks Tags 00HI and 00HB)

proof.text:
Fix a prime $\mathfrak u\subset A$ and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak u\cap R$, $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-finite-separable-fibres],
$$A\otimes_R k\cong\prod_{i=1}^r L_i,\qquad L_i=\kappa(\mathfrak u_i),$$
where the $\mathfrak u_i$ are all primes over $\mathfrak p$, and $L_i/k$ is separable algebraic. Here $r\geq1$ because $\mathfrak u$ is one of them. [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] identifies
$$E=B\otimes_R k\cong B\otimes_A(A\otimes_R k).$$
Let $e_i$ be the images in $E$ of the coordinate idempotents of $\prod L_i$. They are orthogonal and sum to $1$. Thus $E\to\prod e_iE$, $z\mapsto(e_iz)_i$, has inverse $(z_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i z_i$. Tensoring the projection onto $L_i$ identifies $e_iE$ with $E_i=B\otimes_A L_i$: the maps send $b\otimes l$ to $b$ times the $i$-coordinate element $l$, and $e_i(b\otimes(a_j)_j)$ to $b\otimes a_i$. These are mutually inverse by the tensor balancing relations.

source.place: Tag 0AH1 (lemma-filtered-colimit-etale-noetherian-fibres); finite-product idempotents and the displayed tensor calculation

proof.text: Step 3 says $E$ is geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Each factor $E_i$ is geometrically regular over $k$: after any finite field extension $k'/k$, the orthogonal-idempotent decomposition remains a finite product. A prime of a finite product contains all but one of its coordinate idempotents (since distinct ones multiply to zero); localization at that prime is exactly the localization of that one factor. Hence every prime-local ring of $E_i\otimes_k k'$ is regular local because it is a prime-local ring of the regular ring $E\otimes_k k'$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The factor is Noetherian as a quotient of that Noetherian ring. This proves geometric regularity of $E_i$ over $k$ directly. Now [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-regularity-separable-extension] applies to the separable algebraic extension $k\subset L_i$ and the Noetherian $L_i$-algebra $E_i$, and gives geometric regularity over $L_i$. Taking $\mathfrak u_i=\mathfrak u$ proves the required geometric regularity of every fibre of $A\to B$. Together with step 4 this proves regularity of the induced strict-local morphism.

For the dimension assertion let $\mathfrak v\subset B$ represent $v$, $\mathfrak u=\mathfrak v\cap A$ represent $u$, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak v\cap S$ represent $y$, and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak u\cap R=\mathfrak q\cap R$ represent $x$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to $R\to A$ at $\mathfrak u$, and to $S\to B$ at $\mathfrak v$. These maps are flat by step 2. Their local fibres are fields: [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-finite-separable-fibres] identifies the full fibres with finite products of fields, and localization at the selected prime keeps its field factor. A field has only the zero prime, so its dimension is zero. Consequently
$$\dim A_{\mathfrak u}=\dim R_{\mathfrak p},\qquad \dim B_{\mathfrak v}=\dim S_{\mathfrak q}.$$
All rings in these formulas are Noetherian by step 1; their local dimensions are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-system-of-parameters].

source.place: Tags 00ON (algebra.tex lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total), 0AH1 and 00KD (Noetherian local dimension bound)

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] also to the flat maps $A\to B$ (step 4) and $R\to S$ (the hypothesis on $h$) at $\mathfrak v,\mathfrak q$. This gives
$$\dim B_{\mathfrak v}=\dim A_{\mathfrak u}+\dim(B_{\mathfrak v}/\mathfrak uB_{\mathfrak v}),$$
$$\dim S_{\mathfrak q}=\dim R_{\mathfrak p}+\dim(S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}).$$
Substitute step 7 and cancel the equal finite base dimensions. The two quotient dimensions are equal. By [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] these quotients are respectively $\mathcal O_{(Y_{(\bar y)})_u,v}$ and $\mathcal O_{Y_x,y}$. This is the stated equality for every $v$, including nonclosed points.

For ordinary localizations, replace $A,B$ by $R,S$ themselves, the local rings at the compatible ordinary points $x_0,y_0$. Their excellence and Noetherianity were already checked in step 1, and their induced map is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal]. A point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ (respectively $\operatorname{Spec}S$) represents a generalization $x$ of $x_0$ (respectively $y$ of $y_0$), and its local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ (respectively $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$): localizing a ring at a prime and then at a prime above it inverts precisely the elements outside the latter prime. The corresponding stalk map is unchanged. Thus [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] identifies both local fibre rings with the same quotient $\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_x\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, proving the ordinary-local dimension assertion.

source.place: Tag 07C0 (lemma-regular-local); transitivity of localization and Tag 0HA1

proof.text: Finally write $C=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, using the affine description of a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the fibre product is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AA/I)$, which is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/IB)$: on coordinates $b\otimes(a+I)\mapsto ab+IB$ gives $B\otimes_A A/I\cong B/IB$, inverse $b+IB\mapsto b\otimes1$. The base change $A/I\to B/IB$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change], applied to the regular $A\to B$ of step 6. Its finite-type base-change hypothesis holds: the quotient $A/I$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by the empty set, regardless of the size of $I$. Both quotients are Noetherian excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], taking the finite type quotient algebra and multiplicative subset $\{1\}$. This proves the last clause; $I=A$ gives the empty closed subscheme and is included.
